blocks.text: *Gear that shapes your skills, your defense, and your look.*
Weapons decide which skills you may use

Your weapon is more than a stat stick — its **type** decides which of the skills you have learned you may use right now (see *Skills*), and a forged weapon raises one of those skills through its **trademark** (below). Every weapon is a real 3D object your character holds.
The weapon roster

Every weapon owns a **distinct playstyle** — one clear reason to wield it. That playstyle isn't a design label: each of the fourteen is what the artist kept of one of the **Fourteen Kashira**, and how the weapon fights *is* how that Kashira fought (see **The World of Unwritten** and **The Whole Story**). **Mastery raises** lists the three stats that grow as your mastery of that weapon does — +0.5% each per mastery level. They fall into four families:
Might — physical power, up close

rows: Wide cleaves that hit every enemy in a broad arc; built to wipe out packs, not to duel.
Control enemies by denying their actions.
Stuns and knocks back, interrupting what enemies were about to do.
Pulls enemies in, dashes through their line, and cuts the defence of whatever it moves.
Overwhelm with physical bursts, or stand in front and take the hits — or both.

Two paths, chosen by the skills you learn. **Offence:** builds energy, then spends all your MP on one enormous physical blow; energy blasts that still deal physical damage. **Defence:** taunts, cuts damage taken, blocks, sends damage back. Build one path or mix both.

blocks.text: Finesse — precision & mobility

rows: Slows enemies and dashes away to keep its distance; fights on the move.
Kill slowly with poison from the blade.
Stacks poison on one target with every hit; the poison does its damage over time.
Nysara, the Face Without a Name
Finish targets with chains of critical hits.
Raises its crit chance and crit damage as the fight goes on; finishes low-health targets.

blocks.text: Arcane — magic

rows: Area nukes, Burn, and Freeze and slows to lock an area down.
Heals, regeneration, damage shields, buffs, and Cleanse.

blocks.text: Hybrid — two families in one

rows: Win duels through precise single-target bursts and timed defence.
Fast strike combos that burst one enemy down; parries and braces at the right moment to win the exchange.
Stacks Bleed; gains speed and a damage buff that keeps rising while it keeps attacking; gives up all defence to do it.
Many blades: thrown, they bounce through a crowd; swung, one swing lands two or three times.

**Thrown:** normal attacks, and some skills, bounce to nearby enemies. **Swung:** each swing can hit two or three times, and never bounces; its signature blow drops your HP to 1 for one huge physical hit.
melee or ranged — whichever of your STR or DEX is higher
Silence, defence cut and mana drain that wear an enemy down over a long fight.
Land one painful shot from as far away as possible.
One magic shot that can crit — the only magic in the game that can; the further the target, the more it hurts; the longest reach in the game.

blocks.text: Each weapon type has a deep pool of skills, but **a weapon carries none of them**. You learn a skill by spending that kind of weapon's mastery points on it, and it is yours for good — what you hold only decides which of the ones you know you may use right now. See *Skills* for how they are learned.
Equipment slots
Beyond your weapon, you wear:

items: **Head**, **Body**, **Garment** and **Shoes** — each in **metal**, **leather** or **cloth**. There is no off-hand: blocking and sending damage back come from the Fist's defence skills.

blocks.text: Every armour piece rolls **one word** when it is forged, from its own slot's words, and wears it in its name — *+15 Tireless Iron Sabatons [C]*. A word does one thing, grows with the piece's grade, and never changes. No word appears on two slots, so you can never wear the same word twice.

rows: Fewer critical hits land on you
Stuns, freezes, silences and ailments on you end sooner
Less damage from Fire · Water · Earth · Wind
Knockbacks and pulls move you a shorter distance

blocks.text: There is no ring slot: your **Ring** is part of you, not something you wear (see *Stats & the Ring*).

Each piece adds what its **folds** and its **quality** make it worth — attack on a weapon; on armour, what its material buys — plus its word, plus any stats written onto it with **Ink** (see *Crafting & Recycling*).
Folds (+N)

The **+N** on a piece is how many times it has been **folded** at its station. Each fold costs one unit of the band material of the piece's own grade, plus gold, and adds to what the piece is worth: **attack** on a weapon (a staff, wand or scythe gains magic attack instead). On armour, the **material** decides what a fold adds — **metal** defence and HP, **leather** attack speed and evasion, **cloth** magic defence and MP — and a head piece or shoes add half of what body armour or a garment add. **Shoes** also make you move faster: **+2% movement speed for every fold**, whatever they are made of, so +5 shoes are +10%. Bare feet add nothing.

That fold total is then **lifted by the grade** — nothing at Raw and F, rising to **+30% at A**. So an A-grade piece at its full thirty-five folds carries 82 attack, where the same thirty-five folds on an E-grade piece carry 66.
**A quench spends every fold**, whichever way it goes. Folds are not lost work: half of what a finished piece cost comes back if you recycle it (see *Crafting & Recycling*).
Quality

Every piece you make carries a **quality grade**. A freshly forged piece is **Raw**; above that the ladder runs **F, E, D, C, B, A**, and A is the best there is. Quality is decided by the **quench** — the one moment of luck in a whole piece's making — and it moves one rung at a time, up or down, never in a jump.

**Quality decides five things.** How far a piece can be **folded**, which is what its attack — or its armour's material stats — are made of; how much that fold total is **lifted**; how many **stats** can be written onto it with Ink; how far your **mastery** with it can go, and how many of a skill's levels count; and, on a weapon, how much its **trademark** raises its skill — **+5%** at Raw up to **+20%** at A. A fine blade does not swing harder by itself — it lets you become better with it than a poor one ever will.
Where a weapon's skills come from

**A weapon carries no skills.** You learn them yourself: fighting with that kind of weapon raises its mastery, every mastery level gives one point, and you spend points on its skills. Every skill names the **mastery level** at which it can be bought, and some name a skill that needs a point first. What you have learned is yours for good — the weapon in your hands only decides which of them you may use, how far its mastery can still grow, and how many of each skill's levels count.

**A forged weapon has a trademark.** At the forge it rolls one skill of its type and is named for it — a sword that empowers Thousand Petals is itself called **Thousand Petals**, and folded to +15 at grade C it reads **+15 Thousand Petals [C]** in your bag and on its card. The name never changes. Any skill of the weapon's pool that has a number to raise can come up: each ultimate one time in twenty, the others sharing the rest evenly. While you hold the weapon, **every** number that skill puts out is raised by **+5%** at Raw, rising with the grade to **+20%** at A — a Thousand Petals sword raises Thousand Petals' strike and its damage buff alike. Every trademark skill, on any weapon or none, is also **efficient** one cast in twenty, raising those numbers by a further +20% (see *Skills*). Hover the weapon to see which skill and which numbers; hover the skill to see the bonus on its own line.
So two people holding the same sword do not have the same skills: they have the skills they each chose.
Cards
Some gear has **card slots**. Cards are not in the game yet — see **Cards**.

text: *Status: the 14-weapon roster is locked, and every weapon can be held. The Katar, Shuriken, Wand, Scythe and Sniper borrow a dagger's, a staff's, an axe's or a bow's look until their own models arrive, the Fist fights bare-handed, and every weapon but the Bow, Sniper and Fist swings with the Sword's attack until its own animation does. A Shuriken swings melee or ranged by your higher of STR or DEX, and thrown it bounces through up to 3 more enemies and comes back to your hand; a Sniper's normal attack is a magic shot that can crit and hits 2% harder for every metre to its target; the Shuriken's two-or-three-hit swings and the Fist's and Shuriken's all-in blows come with their skills, which are not in the game yet. Folding, quenching and the quality ladder are built; each weapon type's skill pool is being authored, and only the Sword's is finished today.*
